## Libraries

We will use `tidyverse` suite for data manipulations and plotting, `patchwork` for putting several plots together, and `tikzDevice` for rendering to LaTeX. For mathematical symbol's rendering we'd also add package `amsmath` to the `tikzLatexPackages` options.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(tikzDevice)
options(tikzLatexPackages = c(options()$tikzLatexPackages, "\\usepackage{amsmath}\n"))


```

## Data import

We import both the empirical cumulative distribution functions for $N$ signals, as well as the analytical solutions.

```{r}

ecdf_tbl <- read_csv("ecdf_tbl.csv") %>% mutate(analytical = FALSE)
analytical_cdf_tbl <- read_csv("analytical_cdf_tbl.csv") %>%
  mutate(analytical = TRUE, signal_type = "analytical")

```

## Plotting

The below should be repeated for `selected_n`, which will be saved as separate plots.

We choose to only show certain functions, not to overwhelm the reader. The chosen functions are stored in `funs_to_show`. Also we select only certain harmonics in `harmonics_to_show`.

```{r}
# Set the parameter for the converters.
selected_n <- 12

# Set the harmonics we want to show.
harmonics_to_show <- c(1, 7, 11, 19)

# Also which functions do we want to show
funs_to_show <- c("damped_sinusoid", "damped_exponential", "damped_chirp", "lorentzian_pulse",
                  "half_sine_pulse", "gaussian_pulse", "damped_sawtooth", "analytical")
```

```{r}

# Filter the tables.
ecdf_tbl_toplot <- ecdf_tbl %>%
  filter(harmonic_no %in% harmonics_to_show,
         N == selected_n,
         x < selected_n,
         signal_type %in% funs_to_show) %>%
  mutate(signal_type = factor(signal_type, levels = funs_to_show))

analytical_cdf_toplot <- analytical_cdf_tbl %>% 
  filter(N == selected_n, x < selected_n) %>%
  mutate(signal_type = factor(signal_type, levels = funs_to_show))


```

The actual plot. The colors were chosen to contribute nicely to a palette, with the exception of the color for the analytic (theoretical) solution, which was on purpose chosen with a high contrast. The line types and line widths were also changed to differentiate between the analytic and simulation results.

```{r}
# Some plotting parameters
colours <- c("#005F6B", "#E0C097", "#D97B42", 
             "#2D6A4F", "#5B2C6F", "#B22222", 
             "#4169E1", "#FF4500")
legend_labels <- c("Damped sinusoid", "Exponential", "Damped chirp", 
                   "Lorentzian pulse", "Half-sine pulse", "Gaussian pulse",
                   "Sawtooth", "\\textbf{Theoretical}")

ggp <- ggplot(data = ecdf_tbl_toplot,
              mapping = aes(x = x, y = y, 
                            linetype = interaction(analytical, signal_type), 
                            colour = interaction(analytical, signal_type),
                            linewidth = interaction(analytical, signal_type))) +
  geom_step() +
  geom_line(data = analytical_cdf_toplot) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = selected_n - 1, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
           fill = "#FF4500", alpha = 0.2) + 
  labs(x = "$r$", y = "$P(|Z_N[h]| \\leq r)$", linetype = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, selected_n, by = 1), 
                     minor_breaks = seq(0, selected_n, by = 0.5)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(rep("solid", 7), "dashed"), labels = legend_labels) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colours, labels = legend_labels) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(rep(0.4, 7), 0.8), guide = NULL) +
  facet_grid(harmonic_no~., 
             labeller = as_labeller(\(l) str_c("$h =", as.character(l), "$"))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 6.5) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(15, 'pt'),
        legend.key.height = unit(7, 'pt'),
        legend.margin = margin(t = -5, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0)
        ) 

show(ggp)

```

### Save to `.tex` and export to `.pdf`

```{r}
filename <- str_interp("ecdf_N${selected_n}.tex")
tikz(filename, standAlone = TRUE, height = 3.3, width = 3.3, pointsize = 8)
ggp
dev.off()

system(str_interp("pdflatex ${filename}"))
```

# Examples of signals

I also want to show examples of signals (in time domain) for this paper.

```{r}
lf <- list.files("../example_signals/", pattern = ".csv")
# Read signals and add the information about signal type.
signals <- map_dfr(lf, function(.filename) {
  signal_example <- read_csv(file.path("../example_signals/", .filename)) 
  signal_example <- mutate(signal_example, 
                           signal_type = str_match(.filename, "([a-z]+)_example.csv")[,2])
  return(signal_example)
})

funs_to_show <- c("sinusoid", "exponential", 
                  "chirp", "lorentzian",
                  "sine", "gaussian", "sawtooth")
signals <- filter(signals, signal_type %in% funs_to_show)
signals <- mutate(signals, signal_type = factor(signal_type, levels = funs_to_show))

```

Now, let's plots them. Some initial parameters to be reused.

```{r}
colours <- c("#005F6B", "#E0C097", "#D97B42", 
             "#2D6A4F", "#5B2C6F", "#B22222", 
             "#4169E1")
legend_labels <- c("Damped sinusoid", "Exponential", "Damped chirp", 
                   "Lorentzian pulse", "Half-sine pulse", "Gaussian pulse",
                   "Sawtooth")
facet_labels <-  c("Damped\nsinusoid", "Exponential", "Damped\nchirp", 
                   "Lorentzian\npulse", "Half-sine\npulse", "Gaussian\npulse",
                   "Sawtooth")
names(legend_labels) <- funs_to_show
names(facet_labels) <- funs_to_show
```

Now, the plot itself.

```{r}

ggp <- signals %>%
  ggplot(aes(time, amplitude, colour = signal_type)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(signal_type ~ ., scales = "free",
             labeller = labeller(signal_type = facet_labels)) +
  labs(x = "Time (s)", y = "Amplitude", colour = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colours, labels = legend_labels) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 6.5) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(15, 'pt'),
        legend.key.height = unit(7, 'pt'),
        legend.margin = margin(t = -5, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0),
        strip.text.y = element_text(size = 4.5, angle = 0)) 

```

```{r}

filename <- "signal_examples.tex"
tikz(filename, standAlone = TRUE, height = 3.6, width = 3.3, pointsize = 8)
ggp
dev.off()

system(str_interp("pdflatex ${filename}"))

```

## Harmonics

Let's also plot the magnitude of the harmonics.

```{r}
Fs <- 2000 # Sampling frequency
signals_fft <- group_by(signals, signal_type)
signals_fft <- mutate(signals_fft, 
                      icm = fft(amplitude),
                      freq = 0: (n()-1) * Fs/n(),
                      icm_mag = 2 * Mod(icm) / n())
signals_fft <- slice(signals_fft, 1:(n()/2))
signals_fft <- filter(signals_fft, freq %% 10 == 0)
signals_fft <- ungroup(signals_fft)


```

Plot

```{r}

ggp <- ggplot(signals_fft, aes(freq, icm_mag, colour = signal_type, fill = signal_type)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.1) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 500)) +
    facet_grid(signal_type ~ ., scales = "free",
             labeller = labeller(signal_type = facet_labels)) +
  labs(x = "Frequency (Hz)", y = "$|I_{\\text{CM}}[h]|$", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colours, labels = legend_labels) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colours, labels = legend_labels) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 6.5) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(15, 'pt'),
        legend.key.height = unit(7, 'pt'),
        legend.margin = margin(t = -5, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0),
        strip.text.y = element_text(size = 4.5, angle = 0)) 

```

```{r}
filename <- "signal_examples_fft.tex"
tikz(filename, standAlone = TRUE, height = 3.6, width = 3.3, pointsize = 8)
ggp
dev.off()

system(str_interp("pdflatex ${filename}"))

```
